title: Who holds the keys?
briefing: Only members of the sudo group can become root. Who are they?
The answer is in /etc/group — one line per group, members in the last field.
tips: `grep '^sudo:' /etc/group` finds the sudo line; `cut -d: -f4` is its member list.
objective: Find which account is a member of the sudo group and write that username into ~/admin.txt.
hints: Each group is a line in /etc/group ending in a comma-separated member list. Find the sudo line.
`grep '^sudo:' /etc/group` gives the line; the 4th colon-field is the members: `cut -d: -f4`.
explanation: /etc/group maps group names to their members. Membership in sudo/wheel is the difference between an ordinary user and an administrator. Knowing who has that power — and limiting it — is core to securing a system.
